comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIX SHAPE — and why it is deliberately NOT "fail health when the store is missing".

The obvious reading of this ticket is "make /health fail when there is no store". That would be
actively dangerous to land right now, and the reason is worth recording.

The production box TODAY has no store (sibling ticket kilted-nuclear-bronco). /health is BOTH the
container HEALTHCHECK (Dockerfile.mcp:56-57) and the blue-green readiness gate
(autodeploy.sh:130). So a health check that fails on a missing store would, on the very next
deploy, mark the currently-SERVING mcp container unhealthy, cause autodeploy to refuse promotion,
and — with `restart: always` — put the boot container into a restart loop. The endpoint works
today; a change whose purpose is to REPORT a problem must not be the thing that causes an outage.

So the shape is:

1. /health REPORTS store status and keeps returning 200:
     {"in_flight": N, "store": {"path": ..., "present": bool, "expected": bool}}
   `expected` is true only when a tracker dir is EXPLICITLY configured. That is the discriminator
   the ticket's AC1 asks for — "distinguishes serving with a usable store from serving with no
   store" — without conflating "this deployment has no store" with "this deployment is broken".

2. The autodeploy readiness gate enforces `store.present` only when `store.expected` is true.
   Today mcp sets no tracker dir => expected=false => the gate is INERT and nothing can break.
   Once kilted-nuclear-bronco sets REBAR_TRACKER_DIR => expected=true => the gate becomes strict
   automatically, with no second change and no flag day.

3. Boot logs one line naming the store path and whether it was found (AC2). Today
   mcp_server.py:759-761 guards the ensure-sweep with `if os.path.isdir(_tracker)` and emits
   NOTHING when absent — the comment at :752 ("a missing store ... never aborts boot") is a
   reasonable posture, but combined with a health probe that cannot see the store it is why this
   failure went unobserved since deployment. Keep the log-and-continue posture; just make it say
   something.

This makes the two tickets order-independent by construction: whichever lands first, neither can
break the box. That is the point of keying on `expected` rather than on presence alone.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implemented as Gerrit 2232, in the report-not-fail shape argued above.

- /health now returns {"in_flight": N, "store": {"path", "present", "expected"}} and still
  200s. store_status() never raises: a probe that can throw would turn a store-resolution
  problem into a restart loop under `restart: always`, which is the opposite of reporting it.
- autodeploy readiness gate refuses to promote on `expected AND NOT present`, with a named
  mcp-store-missing error. Gated on expected, NOT presence alone — that is the property that
  makes this safe to land while the box still has no store. An older container whose /health
  predates the field reports neither key and is treated as not-expected, so a mixed-version
  deploy cannot be blocked by it.
- mcp_server boot emits one WARNING naming the store path when absent (AC2). The
  log-and-continue posture is kept; it just says something now.

IMPLEMENTATION NARROWING: `expected` reads the REBAR_TRACKER_DIR env override alone, not the
parsed config. The repo's check_config_ownership gate reserves load_config to approved seams,
and coupling a health probe to config parsing is a bad idea independently. A project that
instead declares a non-default tracker.dir in config reports expected=False and simply does not
get the strict gate — it degrades to the old behaviour rather than misreporting. The deployment
surface that matters here sets the env var explicitly.

Mutation-checked: hard-coding `expected` to True — the exact mistake that would cause the
outage this shape avoids — turns test_no_configured_dir_is_not_expected RED.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LANDING HAZARD — this change must NOT land before the store actually works. Plan review
caught a factual error in my safety argument and it turns out to matter operationally.

I wrote: 'the production box today sets no tracker dir, so expected is false, so the gate is
INERT and cannot refuse a healthy container.' That was TRUE when written and became FALSE when
kilted-nuclear-bronco (Gerrit 2231) merged and deployed — that change sets
REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets on the mcp service. Verified on the live
container just now:

    REBAR_TRACKER_DIR on the live container: /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets   -> expected = TRUE
    store present?                            NO                            -> present  = FALSE

That is precisely the gate's refusal condition. If this change deployed today the readiness gate
would refuse to promote EVERY mcp container with mcp-store-missing, blocking all mcp deploys
until the store is repaired. The gate would be doing exactly what it was designed to do; the
mistake is mine, in reasoning about inertness from a premise that a sibling change had already
invalidated.

CONSEQUENCE, recorded as a dependency: this ticket now depends_on fathomable-yester-thrip (the
poisoned-volume fix, Gerrit 2244). The store on the box is currently a 1.5GB partial clone with
no resolvable HEAD; until a real clone lands, expected=true/present=false is the steady state
and this gate must not go live.

The gate logic itself is unchanged and correct — keying on expected AND NOT present is still the
right condition, and the three harness tests still pass. What changed is only WHEN it is safe to
enable, and that is now enforced by the link rather than by a paragraph.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`/health` on the MCP server returns 200 without ever touching the ticket store, so a container
with **no store at all** passes both the container HEALTHCHECK and the blue-green readiness
gate. A structurally broken deploy is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

## Evidence

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:118-120` — the handler returns `JSONResponse({"in_flight": gauge.value})`
  and nothing else.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:56-57` — the container HEALTHCHECK is a plain 200 check on
  `/health`.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:130` — the blue-green readiness gate promotes on that same probe.
- `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:759-761` — the boot sweep is guarded by `if os.path.isdir(_tracker)`
  and emits NOTHING when the store is absent; the comment at `:752` states the intent
  ("a missing store / import / sweep error never aborts boot"), so not even the `debug` line at
  `:769` fires (that needs an exception).

Corroborating log evidence: 60 SSM invocations spanning 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-25 contain zero
matches for `tickets-tracker`, `not initialized`, or `ticket init` — exactly what the code
predicts. (Container logs use `driver: journald` at `docker-compose.yml:72,258,306,383` and no
CloudWatch log group exists for them, so there is no remote log trail either.)

## Why this matters

This is the reason the missing-store defect went unnoticed since deployment. Log-and-continue on
boot is a defensible posture on its own; combining it with a health probe that cannot observe the
store means nothing in the pipeline can ever report the failure.

## How `expected` is computed (the field the whole refusal turns on)

`expected` is TRUE iff the deployment has EXPLICITLY declared where its store lives — concretely
`config.tracker_dir_override()`, i.e. the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` env override is set and non-empty.
It is FALSE when nothing is configured and the path is merely the default relative
`.tickets-tracker` resolved against the repo root.

Deliberately read from the ENV OVERRIDE ALONE, not the parsed config, for two reasons: a health
probe must not be able to fail (or hang) on config parsing, and the repo's
`check_config_ownership` gate reserves `load_config` to approved seams. A project that instead
declares a non-default `tracker.dir` in config therefore reports `expected: false` and simply
does not get the strict gate — it degrades to the pre-change behaviour rather than misreporting.
The deployment surface that matters here (the mcp compose service) sets the env var explicitly.

This is what makes the safety story concrete — and the STATE OF THE BOX MATTERS, so state it
as of now rather than as a standing property. When this was first written the mcp service set
no tracker dir, so `expected` was false and the gate was inert. That is NO LONGER TRUE: the
sibling change kilted-nuclear-bronco now sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`,
verified on the live container. The store is meanwhile absent (a partial clone with no
resolvable HEAD), so the box currently sits at `expected=true, present=false` — exactly the
refusal condition.

The gate is therefore LIVE, not inert, and landing this before the store works would refuse
promotion of every mcp container with `mcp-store-missing`, blocking mcp deploys entirely. That
is the gate behaving as designed; the ordering is the thing that must be controlled. This
ticket accordingly `depends_on` fathomable-yester-thrip (the poisoned-volume fix) and must not
land until a real clone is in place.

## What `present` means, and why it is not HEAD-strict

`present` is exactly `os.path.isdir(path)` — the directory exists. It is deliberately NOT "a
usable store" (a resolvable HEAD), and that choice is load-bearing:

Provisioning is BACKGROUNDED (`provision_store &` then `exec "$@"`) because the ~200k-commit
clone outruns the 120s blue-green readiness deadline. A freshly started container therefore has
a legitimately empty, HEAD-less tracker dir for MINUTES while its clone runs. A HEAD-strict
`present` would report that healthy container as not-ready, the gate would roll it back, and
the next tick would start another — reproducing the rollback loop `unfit-beneficial-whimbrel`
documents. The probe answers "is a store dir here at all", not "is it converged".

**Residual limitation, stated rather than implied:** a POISONED store — files but no usable
`.git`, the state observed in production — satisfies `isdir` and reports `present: True`. This
probe does not detect that and is not the mechanism that should: `fathomable-yester-thrip`
(change 2244, merged) re-clones a store whose HEAD does not resolve. This gate catches the
ABSENT-store deploy; the entrypoint catches the poisoned-store deploy. Neither subsumes the
other, and the acceptance criteria below are scoped to the absent case only.

## Acceptance Criteria

All proven by `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py` (8 tests), each mutation-checked.

- [x] `/health` reports the store as a structured object — `{path, present, expected}`.
      Proof: `test_present_store_is_reported_present`,
      `test_absent_store_is_reported_absent_and_expected_when_a_dir_is_configured`
- [x] The gate FAILS OPEN on an unreadable or malformed signal, matching autodeploy's posture.
      Proof: `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`
- [x] The refusal is keyed on `expected AND NOT present`, never on absence alone, so a
      deployment that never configured a tracker dir is not marked unhealthy.
      Proof: `test_no_configured_dir_is_not_expected`
- [x] The refusal is observable under its own name (`mcp-store-missing`).
      Proof: `test_autodeploy_gate_names_the_storeless_refusal`
- [x] Boot emits one log line naming the tracker path when the store is absent, and is quiet
      when it exists. Proof: `test_boot_sweep_warns_naming_the_path_when_the_store_is_absent`,
      `test_boot_sweep_is_quiet_and_does_not_raise_when_the_store_exists`
- [x] `store_status()` never raises for an ordinary resolution fault, with ONE deliberate
      exception: a removed-but-still-set load-bearing input fails hard rather than being
      reported as merely degraded.
      Proof: `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`,
      `test_a_removed_load_bearing_input_fails_hard_instead_of_being_reported` — mutating the
      handler to swallow it yields DID NOT RAISE.


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py -q -p no:randomly
    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py -q -p no:randomly

Per-criterion proving tests:

| criterion | proving test |
|---|---|
| gate consumes the field and refuses | `test_storeless_container_is_not_promoted_when_a_store_is_expected` |
| fails open on a body with no store field | `test_health_without_a_store_field_still_promotes` |
| keyed on expected, not absence | `test_storeless_container_IS_promoted_when_no_store_is_expected` |
| named refusal reason | `test_autodeploy_gate_names_the_storeless_refusal` |
| boot names the absent path | `test_boot_sweep_warns_naming_the_path_when_the_store_is_absent` |
| probe never raises / present-store branch runs | `test_probe_never_raises_even_when_resolution_fails`, `test_boot_sweep_is_quiet_and_does_not_raise_when_the_store_exists` |

Teeth: gating on `present` alone (dropping `expected`) turns the two promote-cases RED; removing
the gate turns the refusal case RED; an early return in the sweep turns the liveness anchor RED.
